events.title: Bang Si-hyuk Assembles BTS Trainees
events.detail: Big Hit Entertainment CEO Bang Si-hyuk begins recruiting members for a new hip-hop oriented boy group. RM (Kim Nam-joon) is the first recruit, signing as a trainee in 2010. Other members are gradually added through auditions, including J-Hope, Suga, Jin, Jimin, V, and Jungkook.

events.title: BTS Officially Debuts with '2 Cool 4 Skool'
events.detail: Bangtan Sonyeondan (BTS) officially debuts on Mnet's M Countdown with their first single album '2 Cool 4 Skool' and lead single 'No More Dream.' The seven-member group — RM, Jin, Suga, J-Hope, Jimin, V, and Jungkook — is signed to Big Hit Entertainment under the creative direction of Bang Si-hyuk.

events.title: 'O!RUL8,2?' Mini Album Released
events.detail: BTS releases their second extended play 'O!RUL8,2?' with the lead single 'N.O.' The album addresses the pressures Korean youth face from societal expectations around education and career paths, establishing the group's signature socially conscious lyrical approach.

events.title: 'Skool Luv Affair' Charts on Billboard World Albums
events.detail: BTS releases their third EP 'Skool Luv Affair' featuring the single 'Boy In Luv.' It becomes their first album to chart on the Billboard World Albums chart, marking their first foothold in the US market and signaling growing international interest.

events.title: Debut Studio Album 'Dark & Wild' Released
events.detail: BTS releases their debut full-length studio album 'Dark & Wild' featuring 14 tracks. The album enters the US Billboard Heatseekers chart and demonstrates the group's expansion beyond their school-era concept into darker, more mature themes.

events.title: Japan Debut Album 'Wake Up' Expands Asian Reach
events.detail: BTS releases their first Japanese studio album 'Wake Up,' expanding their presence in the Japanese market — a crucial revenue source for K-pop acts. The album includes Japanese versions of Korean hits alongside new material.

events.title: 'The Most Beautiful Moment in Life Pt. 1' Released
events.detail: BTS releases the first part of the 'Hwa Yang Yeon Hwa' (The Most Beautiful Moment in Life) series. The mini album features 'I Need U,' exploring themes of youth, pain, and fleeting beauty. The concept marks BTS's artistic maturation beyond the school trilogy.

events.title: 'HYYH Pt. 2' Achieves First Billboard 200 Entry
events.detail: BTS releases 'The Most Beautiful Moment in Life Pt. 2,' featuring the single 'Run.' The album marks BTS's first ever entry on the Billboard 200 US chart at No. 171, signaling a growing Western fanbase and hinting at their future global dominance.

events.title: 'Wings' Debuts at No. 26 on Billboard 200 — K-pop Record
events.detail: BTS releases their second studio album 'Wings,' featuring solo and sub-unit tracks for the first time. The album enters the Billboard 200 at No. 26 — the highest-charting K-pop album in US history at the time — demonstrating their explosive global growth.

events.title: BTS Wins First Billboard Music Award, Beating Justin Bieber
events.detail: BTS wins the Top Social Artist award at the Billboard Music Awards in Las Vegas, defeating Justin Bieber who had won the title for six consecutive years. This is the first time a K-pop act wins at the BBMAs and marks BTS's breakthrough into US mainstream consciousness.

events.title: 'Love Yourself: Her' Peaks at No. 7 on Billboard 200
events.detail: BTS releases 'Love Yourself: Her' featuring global hit 'DNA,' which charts in 54 countries simultaneously. The album debuts at No. 7 on the Billboard 200 — the highest position ever for a K-pop album at that time — and sets streaming records across all major platforms.

events.title: BTS Becomes First Korean Act to Perform at the AMAs
events.detail: BTS becomes the first Korean act to perform at the American Music Awards, performing 'DNA' to an audience of 10,000+ in Los Angeles. The nationally televised performance introduces BTS to tens of millions of American viewers for the first time.

events.title: 'Love Yourself: Tear' — First K-pop Album to Top Billboard 200
events.detail: BTS's fourth studio album 'Love Yourself: Tear' debuts at No. 1 on the Billboard 200, making BTS the first K-pop act to ever top the US albums chart. The album sells over 135,000 album-equivalent units in its first week in the US alone.

events.title: 'Love Yourself: Answer' Reaches No. 1 — Second Consecutive Billboard Topper
events.detail: BTS releases 'Love Yourself: Answer,' a repackage album capping the Love Yourself series. It becomes their second consecutive No. 1 album on the Billboard 200, including the new track 'Idol' which celebrates Korean cultural identity.

events.title: Love Yourself World Tour Launches in Seoul
events.detail: BTS begins the 'Love Yourself World Tour' with sold-out shows at the Olympic Main Stadium in Seoul. The tour ultimately spans 62 concerts in 14 countries across North America, Europe, and Asia, attended by over 2 million fans and grossing $196.4 million.

events.title: RM Addresses 73rd UN General Assembly: 'Speak Yourself'
events.detail: BTS leader RM addresses the 73rd UN General Assembly in New York City on behalf of UNICEF's Generation Unlimited initiative. His speech — urging young people to 'speak yourself' — is viewed by tens of millions online and marks BTS's entry into global diplomatic and humanitarian engagement.

events.title: 'Map of the Soul: Persona' — Third No. 1 Billboard 200 Album
events.detail: BTS releases 'Map of the Soul: Persona' featuring 'Boy With Luv' ft. Halsey. The album debuts at No. 1 on the Billboard 200 and sells 3.4 million copies in South Korea in two months — the best-selling album in South Korean history at the time.

events.title: 'Speak Yourself' Tour Breaks Rose Bowl All-Time Gross Record
events.detail: BTS begins the 'Love Yourself: Speak Yourself' stadium tour with shows at the Rose Bowl in Pasadena, CA. The two-night run becomes the highest-grossing event in Rose Bowl history with 100,000+ attendees across two nights.

events.title: BTS Sets Record as First Korean Act to Sell Out US Arenas
events.detail: During their early 2019 US dates, BTS sells out every US arena on the Love Yourself World Tour, consistently drawing 18,000–20,000 per night. They become the first Korean act to headline and sell out major US arenas at this scale across multiple cities.

events.title: BTS Becomes First Korean Act to Sell Out Wembley Stadium
events.detail: BTS sells out Wembley Stadium in London for two consecutive nights (June 1–2, 2019). They become the first Korean act and first non-English-speaking act to headline Wembley Stadium — a legendary milestone in global music history.

events.title: Love Yourself World Tour Concludes: $196.4M Gross
events.detail: The Love Yourself World Tour concludes after 62 concerts in 14 countries, attended by over 2 million fans worldwide. The tour grosses $196.4 million, placing BTS among the world's top-grossing touring acts and setting a new standard for K-pop live performances.

era: Map of the Soul & COVID-19 Pivot (2020)

events.title: 'Map of the Soul: 7' Sells 4.1 Million Copies in 9 Days
events.detail: BTS releases 'Map of the Soul: 7' — their fourth consecutive No. 1 album on the Billboard 200. The album sells 4.1 million copies worldwide in its first nine days, breaking all K-pop records. The 39-date Map of the Soul Tour is subsequently cancelled due to COVID-19.

events.title: Map of the Soul World Tour Cancelled Due to COVID-19
events.detail: BTS announces the cancellation of their entire 39-show Map of the Soul World Tour due to the global COVID-19 pandemic. The cancellation affects hundreds of thousands of ticket holders and represents a massive financial loss, forcing the group to pivot to virtual concerts.

events.title: 'Dynamite' Debuts at No. 1 — First Korean Act Atop Billboard Hot 100
events.detail: 'Dynamite,' BTS's first fully English-language single, debuts at No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100 — making BTS the first Korean act ever to top the US singles chart. Released August 21, it spends three weeks at No. 1 and becomes a global pandemic anthem, viewed 100M+ times on YouTube in its first 24 hours.

events.title: 'Life Goes On' — First Korean-Language Song to Debut at No. 1 on Hot 100
events.detail: 'Life Goes On' from their album BE debuts at No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100 — the first Korean-language song ever to debut at number one on the chart. The pandemic-themed song resonates globally as a message of hope and resilience.

events.title: 'BE' Album Released — Members Direct Their Own Chapters
events.detail: BTS releases 'BE,' an album with significant member creative control — each member choosing their own concepts, aesthetics, and a track to direct. Created during COVID-19, the album reflects on longing, connection, and what it means to be an artist during a global crisis.

events.title: BTS Named IFPI Global Recording Artist of the Year
events.detail: BTS is named the IFPI Global Recording Artist of the Year for 2020 — the most consumed recording act worldwide across all formats. This is the first time any Korean artist or group wins this distinction, representing a defining moment for K-pop globally.

events.title: BTS Address 75th UN General Assembly on COVID-19
events.detail: BTS deliver a pre-recorded video message at the 75th UN General Assembly, speaking to global youth on hope and resilience during the COVID-19 pandemic — their second UN appearance in three years.

events.title: BTS Receives First Grammy Nomination for 'Dynamite'
events.detail: BTS receives their first Grammy Award nomination — Best Pop Duo/Group Performance for 'Dynamite' at the 63rd Grammy Awards. While they do not win, it marks the first Grammy recognition for any Korean act in history.

events.title: First Korean Act to Perform at the Grammy Awards
events.detail: BTS performs 'Dynamite' at the 63rd Grammy Awards ceremony at Gyeongbokgung Palace in Seoul, becoming the first Korean act to perform on the Grammy stage. The global broadcast is viewed by hundreds of millions of viewers worldwide.

events.title: 'Butter' Spends 10 Weeks at No. 1 on Hot 100
events.detail: BTS releases 'Butter,' which spends a combined 10 weeks at No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100 — a 2021 record. They also become the fastest group to accumulate four US No. 1 singles since the Jackson 5 in 1970.

events.title: 'Permission to Dance' — Fifth Hot 100 No. 1, Matching Beatles Milestone
events.detail: 'Permission to Dance' replaces 'Butter' at No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100, giving BTS their fifth number-one hit. They become the first act since The Beatles to have their first five No. 1 singles all debut at the top of the chart.

events.title: BTS Address 76th UN General Assembly as Presidential Envoys
events.detail: BTS speaks at the UN's SDG Moment at the 76th General Assembly in New York. The group is appointed South Korea's Special Presidential Envoys for Future Generations and Culture by President Moon Jae-in — their most significant diplomatic role to date.

events.title: 'My Universe' with Coldplay — Sixth Hot 100 No. 1
events.detail: 'My Universe,' a collaboration between BTS and Coldplay, debuts at No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100 — the first collaboration between two groups to debut at No. 1. BTS becomes the fastest act since The Beatles to accumulate six US No. 1 singles.

events.title: SoFi Stadium Run Grosses $33.3M — Biggest Boxscore in Nearly a Decade
events.detail: BTS plays four sold-out nights at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, CA (Nov 27–Dec 2, 2021) as part of 'Permission to Dance on Stage.' The run grosses $33.3 million from 214,000 tickets — the biggest concert boxscore by any act in nearly a decade.

era: PTD On Stage, AMA Win & Hiatus (2021–2022)

events.title: First Asian Act to Win AMA Artist of the Year
events.detail: BTS wins Artist of the Year at the American Music Awards 2021 — the first Asian act ever to win this prestigious honor. They also win Favorite Pop Duo or Group and Favorite Pop Song, completing a three-award sweep at the ceremony.

events.title: BTS Wins IFPI Global Recording Artist of the Year for Second Consecutive Year
events.detail: BTS is named IFPI Global Recording Artist of the Year for 2021, becoming the first act to win in two consecutive years since the award's inception. The achievement underscores their unparalleled global cultural reach.

events.title: 'Permission to Dance on Stage' Las Vegas Concludes to 200,000+ Fans
events.detail: BTS closes their 'Permission to Dance on Stage' concert series with four sold-out nights at Allegiant Stadium in Las Vegas (April 8–16, 2022), totaling over 200,000 attendees. These are their first in-person US concerts since 2019.

events.title: 'Proof' Released; BTS Announces Hiatus for Solo Chapter
events.detail: BTS releases 'Proof,' a three-disc anthology album marking the close of 'Chapter 1.' At their FESTA dinner video, members announce a hiatus to pursue individual solo activities. Suga says directly: 'We're going on a hiatus now.' HYBE's stock drops approximately 25% the following trading day.

events.title: Big Hit Entertainment Rebrands as HYBE; IPO Raises $819M
events.detail: Big Hit Entertainment rebrands as HYBE Corporation following its October 2020 IPO on the Korea Stock Exchange, which raised approximately $819 million and valued the company at $4 billion. BTS holds a significant ownership stake, making them among the wealthiest pop stars in South Korea.

events.title: J-Hope Releases First BTS Solo LP; Headlines Lollapalooza
events.detail: J-Hope releases 'Jack in the Box,' the first full-length solo studio album by any BTS member. He headlines Lollapalooza in Chicago on July 31, 2022 — the first South Korean artist ever to headline the iconic festival, playing to 100,000 attendees.

events.title: RM Releases Debut Solo Album 'Indigo'
events.detail: RM releases 'Indigo,' his first solo studio album featuring collaborations with Erykah Badu, Anderson .Paak, and Epik High's Tablo. Described as a document of his late twenties, the album debuts in the top five of multiple global charts.

events.title: Jimin's 'Like Crazy' — First Korean Solo Artist Atop Billboard Hot 100
events.detail: Jimin releases his debut solo album 'FACE,' whose lead single 'Like Crazy' debuts at No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100 — making Jimin the first Korean solo artist ever to top the chart. He also becomes the first Korean solo artist to top the Billboard Artist 100.

events.title: Suga Releases 'D-DAY' as Agust D; Launches World Tour
events.detail: Suga (as Agust D) releases 'D-Day,' completing his Agust D trilogy. The album features IU, J-Hope, and the late Ryuichi Sakamoto. The accompanying 28-show 'D-Day' world tour ranks 9th on Pollstar's 2023 Top 20 Global Concert Tours by average gross.

events.title: V Releases Debut Solo Album 'Layover'
events.detail: V (Kim Tae-hyung) releases his debut solo mini album 'Layover,' a six-track jazz/R&B/pop project with music videos for all tracks. The album showcases V's soulful vocal range and establishes his distinct artistic identity outside the group.

events.title: Jungkook's 'GOLDEN' Becomes Best-Selling K-pop Solo Album in US History
events.detail: Jungkook releases 'GOLDEN' featuring Jack Harlow, Major Lazer, and Latto. Within three weeks, it becomes the best-selling album by a K-pop solo artist in US history by total units, surpassing his bandmates' solo releases.

events.title: RM Releases Second Solo Album 'Right Place, Wrong Person'
events.detail: RM releases his second solo studio album 'Right Place, Wrong Person' while still serving in the military. The album features Little Simz, Domi & JD Beck, and Moses Sumney, reflecting on identity and belonging.

events.title: Jimin's 'MUSE' Surpasses 1 Billion Spotify Streams
events.detail: Jimin releases his second solo album 'MUSE,' whose lead single 'Who' debuts at No. 1 on the Billboard Global 200. The album surpasses 1 billion Spotify streams, making Jimin the first K-pop solo artist with two albums reaching that streaming milestone.

events.title: Jin Becomes First BTS Member to Enlist in Military
events.detail: Jin (Kim Seok-jin) enlists for mandatory South Korean military service on December 13, 2022, becoming the first BTS member to enter the armed forces. The group had been granted a special deferral; with the 'Proof' chapter complete, all members planned to serve.

events.title: J-Hope Enlists; Serves as Assistant Drill Instructor
events.detail: J-Hope enlists on April 18, 2023, serving as an assistant drill instructor at a basic training center. His enlistment follows a banner year for his solo career including Lollapalooza and 'Jack in the Box.'

events.title: Suga Enlists as Social Service Worker Due to Shoulder Surgery
events.detail: Suga enlists as an alternative social service worker on September 22, 2023, due to a prior shoulder surgery that prevents active duty. He is the only BTS member to serve in an alternative capacity rather than active military duty.

events.title: RM, V, Jimin & Jungkook Enlist — All 7 Members Now Serving
events.detail: RM and V enlist simultaneously on December 11; Jimin and Jungkook enlist together on December 12, 2023. With all seven members now in military service, BTS enters the longest pause in its career. RM serves in the Army Band; V in the 2nd Division Special Duty Team.

events.title: Jin Discharged — All Six BTS Members Attend His Greeting
events.detail: Jin completes 18 months of mandatory military service and is discharged on June 12, 2024. All six remaining members — on approved military leave — attend his discharge in a historic moment. Jin later releases his debut solo album 'Happy' (November 2024).

events.title: J-Hope Discharged; Launches Solo World Tour in Early 2025
events.detail: J-Hope is discharged from military service on October 17, 2024. Post-discharge, he releases singles and launches his 'Hope on the Stage' solo world tour in early 2025, playing across Asia and North America.

events.title: Suga Discharged — All 7 BTS Members Complete Military Service
events.detail: Suga completes his alternative social service on June 21, 2025, the last BTS member to finish mandatory service. Within 11 days, all seven members were discharged. HYBE hangs 'We are back' banners on their headquarters. The full reunion is at hand.

events.title: Jin Releases 'Happy' — All 7 Members Now Have Solo Top 10 Billboard Albums
events.detail: Jin releases his debut solo studio album 'Happy' featuring Gary Barlow, Wendy (Red Velvet), and Taka (One Ok Rock). Debuting at No. 4 on the Billboard 200, Jin becomes the last BTS member to release a solo LP, and all seven members have now achieved Billboard 200 top 10 placements.

events.title: BTS Celebrates 12th Debut Anniversary Ahead of Full Reunion
events.detail: BTS celebrates 12 years since their June 13, 2013 debut. With most members discharged or days away from discharge, the anniversary is marked by ARMY worldwide and serves as a prelude to the full group's imminent reunion.

events.title: All 7 Members Reunite on Weverse; New Album & World Tour Announced
events.detail: All seven BTS members appear together in a Weverse livestream watched by over 7 million simultaneous viewers. They announce a new group album and world tour, confirming they have begun collaborative work for the first time since their 2022 hiatus.

events.title: J-Hope Launches 'Hope on the Stage' World Tour Post-Discharge
events.detail: J-Hope launches his 'Hope on the Stage' solo world tour in February 2025, his first major headline tour following his October 2024 military discharge. The tour spans Asia and North America, marking the first major BTS solo live activity of the reunion era.

events.title: BTS Releases 'ARIRANG' — First Group Album in Over 5 Years
events.detail: BTS releases 'ARIRANG,' their 5th full-length studio album — their first since 'BE' in November 2020, a 5-year, 4-month gap. The 14-track album (lead single: 'Swim') is produced by Pdogg, Kevin Parker (Tame Impala), Flume, JPEGMAFIA, Mike WiLL Made-It, and Ryan Tedder. First-day Hanteo sales of 3,981,507 copies — the fastest 1 million copies ever sold (under 10 minutes). All 14 tracks simultaneously occupy the top 14 spots on Spotify Global Top 50. Day 1 Spotify streams: 110 million, setting a new K-pop record and 12th all-time globally.

events.title: BTS Gwanghwamun Comeback Concert — 18.4M Netflix Viewers
events.detail: BTS performs a free public comeback concert at Gwanghwamun Square in Seoul — their first full-group performance since October 2022. 22,000 fans attend via Golden Tickets; approximately 260,000 fill surrounding streets, the largest public concert in South Korean history. Directed by Hamish Hamilton (Super Bowl halftime show). RM performs seated after an ankle injury sustained in rehearsals. The concert livestreams on Netflix as 'BTS: The Comeback Live | Arirang,' reaching 18.4 million viewers and entering the top 10 in 80 countries.

events.title: BTS on The Tonight Show — Two-Night US TV Return
events.detail: BTS appears on The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon for two consecutive nights. Night 1 (March 25): group interview and performance of lead single 'Swim.' Night 2 (March 26): performance of '2.0' at the Guggenheim Museum in New York City — an unannounced special venue set. They also perform at a Spotify fan event in New York during the same week.

events.title: Arirang World Tour Announced — 82 Dates, 34 Cities, 23 Countries
events.detail: BTS announces the Arirang World Tour, their 4th major concert tour: 82 dates across 34 cities in 23 countries (April 2026 – March 2027). Features a 360-degree stage setup. Kick-off: Goyang Stadium, South Korea (April 9–12). Includes Tokyo Dome, North American stadium runs, European arenas, and Southeast Asian dates concluding in Manila (March 2027). Tickets for South Korea, North America, and Europe sell out within hours. Tour revenue projected at up to ₩2.7 trillion (~$1.8 billion USD), comparable to Taylor Swift's Eras Tour.

events.title: 'BTS: The Return' Documentary Premieres on Netflix
events.detail: Netflix releases 'BTS: The Return,' a documentary following the making of the 'ARIRANG' album — from the group's reunion after military service through recording, rehearsals, and the lead-up to the Gwanghwamun comeback concert. The film debuts one week after the album release and concert livestream.

events.title: ARIRANG Confirmed No. 1 on Billboard 200 with 641,000 Units — BTS's 7th #1 Album
events.detail: Billboard confirms ARIRANG debuted at No. 1 on the Billboard 200 (chart dated April 4, 2026) with 641,000 equivalent album units — 532,000 in pure sales. BTS's 7th Billboard 200 No. 1 and the biggest US album debut of 2026. The pure sales figure represents the largest week for any group since One Direction's 'Midnight Memories' in 2013. ARIRANG simultaneously topped charts in Japan, Australia, UK, Canada, and South Korea.

events.title: 'SWIM' Tops Billboard Hot 100 — BTS's 7th No. 1 Single; 13 Tracks Chart Simultaneously
events.detail: Billboard confirms 'Swim' debuted at No. 1 on the Hot 100 (chart dated April 4, 2026) — BTS's 7th Hot 100 No. 1 and first since 2021. BTS becomes the first Korean act to simultaneously top both the Hot 100 and Billboard 200 in the same chart week. 13 of ARIRANG's 14 tracks chart on the Hot 100 simultaneously — a K-pop album record. On the Billboard Global 200, BTS occupies all 13 top positions, the first artist in Billboard history to do so, giving BTS a record 8 No. 1 songs on that chart.

events.title: 'Run BTS 2.0' Announced — Variety Show Returns April 7
events.detail: BTS officially announces the revival of 'Run BTS,' their beloved variety web series (150+ original episodes, 2015–2022), as 'Run BTS 2.0.' The series premieres April 7, 2026 on YouTube and Weverse — concurrent with the Arirang World Tour launch. The original show drew hundreds of millions of views and is credited with connecting ARMY to the members' off-stage personalities.

events.title: ARIRANG Deluxe Vinyl Released — Suga's Hidden Track 'Come Over' Unveiled
events.detail: The ARIRANG Deluxe Vinyl is released on April 3, 2026, introducing a vinyl-exclusive 15th track, 'Come Over,' produced by Suga (with RM and J-Hope credited). The stadium-anthem-meets-pop song features expansive synthesizers, heavy rhythmic beats, and a humming guitar. Available only on the physical vinyl format — not on streaming or CD — the track sparks fan debate over accessibility, though HYBE confirms it is a deliberate collector's exclusive.

events.title: ARIRANG Leads Billboard 200 for Second Week — First K-pop Album to Do So
events.detail: Billboard confirms ARIRANG held #1 on the Billboard 200 (chart dated April 11) for a second consecutive week, earning 187,000 equivalent album units (week ending April 2) — 114,000 pure sales, 65,000 SEA, 8,000 TEA. This makes ARIRANG the first K-pop album in history to spend two consecutive weeks at #1 on the Billboard 200, surpassing all prior BTS titles which each peaked for a single week. Kanye West's 'Bully' debuted at #2.

events.title: Visa Named Worldwide Tour Sponsor for BTS World Tour 'Arirang'
events.detail: Visa announces on April 6, 2026 its role as the Worldwide Tour Sponsor for BTS WORLD TOUR 'ARIRANG' (82 shows, 34 cities, 23 countries). The sponsorship gives Visa cardholders access to ticket giveaways and exclusive booths at eight Asia Pacific venues: Kaohsiung, Bangkok, Kuala Lumpur, Singapore, Jakarta, Sydney, Hong Kong, and Manila. The deal extends Visa's existing K-pop presence, which includes the MAMA Awards.

events.title: Run BTS! 2.0 Premieres — Variety Show Returns After Three-Year Hiatus
events.detail: Run BTS! 2.0 Episode 1 'The Reunion: Back to the Start' premieres April 7, 2026 at 9PM KST on Bangtan TV YouTube and Weverse — free globally. The 45-minute special is filmed at a historic Seoul location echoing the show's 2015 debut episode, featuring a 'Telepathy Test' across all seven members reunited for the first time since 2022. The show's revival runs concurrent with the Arirang World Tour launch, giving ARMY a dual dose of BTS content in their most anticipated comeback week.

events.title: Arirang World Tour Opens in Goyang — Largest K-pop Concert Tour Begins
events.detail: BTS officially opens the ARIRANG World Tour on April 9, 2026 at Goyang Stadium, South Korea — their first full headline concert in three and a half years. Despite rain, 40,000+ fans pack the venue. The show features a 360-degree in-the-round stage with all three Goyang nights sold out (April 9, 11, 12). A global live cinema viewing streams simultaneously to 35+ countries. The tour, spanning 85+ shows across 34 cities in 23 countries through March 2027, is described by HYBE as the largest concert tour by any Korean act in history. Members describe it as 'a totally different stage than before.'

events.title: BTS Returns to Tokyo Dome — First Japan Concerts in Seven Years
events.detail: BTS performs two sold-out nights at Tokyo Dome (April 17–18, 2026) — their first Japan concerts in approximately seven years and the first overseas leg of the Arirang World Tour. Each night features a 360-degree in-the-round stage for ~55,000 fans. Night 1 debuted 'Save Me' and 'Crystal Snow' (first performance since 2018). Night 2 debuted 'Dope' and 'For You' (first since 2018). The April 18 show was live-broadcast to 3,500+ cinemas in 75 countries in partnership with Trafalgar Releasing — a tour first. The run coincides with ARIRANG locking a third consecutive week at No. 1 on the Billboard 200 — a K-pop first.

events.title: HYBE Signs $100M+ Global Distribution Deal with K Wave Media (KWM)
events.detail: K Wave Media Ltd. (KWM) announces an exclusive global distribution agreement with HYBE covering video and merchandise for BTS, SEVENTEEN, LE SSERAFIM, and other HYBE artists, effective April 3, 2026. The deal targets annual revenue exceeding $100 million and adds commercial infrastructure to HYBE's global ARIRANG World Tour push. The announcement coincides with BTS performing at Goyang Stadium; analysts project the ARIRANG World Tour at approximately $1.45 billion in total revenue.

events.title: HYBE Chairman Bang Si-hyuk Faces Arrest — Police Seek Warrant Over Alleged ₩190B IPO Fraud
events.detail: On April 21, 2026, Seoul Metropolitan Police Agency announces it is seeking an arrest warrant for HYBE Chairman and BTS founder Bang Si-hyuk. Police allege Bang defrauded early HYBE investors in 2019 by concealing IPO plans while encouraging them to sell stakes at undervalue to a private equity fund tied to Bang — generating approximately 190 billion won ($129M) in alleged illicit gains after the 2020 HYBE IPO. Bang has been under a travel ban since August 2025 amid a Capital Markets Act investigation. The announcement, covered globally by Bloomberg, Variety, NBC News, and Deadline, represents the most significant legal crisis in HYBE's history. Bang is HYBE's founder and the creative architect behind BTS's global rise. HYBE pledges full cooperation. The warrant request emerges four days before BTS opens the North American leg of the ARIRANG World Tour in Tampa, Florida.

media.caption: Police seek arrest warrant for HYBE Chairman Bang Si-hyuk over ₩190B IPO fraud allegations

events.title: Seoul Prosecutors Reject Bang Si-hyuk Arrest Warrant — HYBE Chairman Cleared of Detention Risk
events.detail: The Seoul Southern District Prosecutors' Office rejected the arrest warrant for HYBE Chairman Bang Si-hyuk on April 24, 2026, citing 'insufficient evidence to justify the necessity of detention.' The Seoul Metropolitan Police Agency had applied for the warrant three days earlier (April 21), alleging Bang defrauded early investors by concealing HYBE's IPO plans in 2019 and enabling a private equity fund linked to Bang to acquire shares at undervalue — allegedly yielding ~260 billion won (~$175M) in illicit gains. Bang has been under a travel ban since August 2025. The rejection provides temporary legal relief the day before BTS opens the North American leg of the ARIRANG World Tour in Tampa, Florida.

media.caption: Seoul prosecutors reject arrest warrant for HYBE Chairman Bang Si-hyuk on April 24, 2026

events.title: Goyang Finale — 'Come Over' Performed Live for the First Time; Korea Opening Run Completes
events.detail: BTS closes the three-night Goyang Stadium opening run on April 12, 2026. The show features the live performance debut of 'Come Over' — the vinyl-exclusive hidden track produced by Suga (RM and J-Hope co-credited) from the ARIRANG Deluxe Vinyl. The production incorporates traditional Korean aesthetics: gayageum melodies, ink-wash painting visuals, and choreography inspired by Seungmu and Ganggangsullae. With the Goyang run complete, the ARIRANG World Tour advances to Tokyo Dome. Korea Times calls the IDOL stadium sequences 'a victory lap that felt almost like a statement of K-pop's global reach.'

events.title: ARIRANG World Tour Lands in North America — Tampa Opening Night Draws 60,000 Fans
events.detail: BTS opens the North American leg of the ARIRANG World Tour on April 25, 2026 at Raymond James Stadium in Tampa, Florida — the first time all seven members have headlined a US stadium together since 2019. Approximately 60,000–65,000 fans attend opening night (first of three sold-out Tampa dates, April 25, 26, and 28; ~180,000 total). The 23-song set opens with 'Hooligan,' 'Aliens,' and 'Run BTS (Remix),' incorporates ARIRANG tracks ('SWIM,' 'Please,' 'Into the Sun,' 'Like Animals,' 'Merry Go Round') alongside classics ('FAKE LOVE,' 'MIC Drop,' 'IDOL,' 'Butter,' 'Dynamite'). Two rotating surprise-song slots close each show. US media coverage compared the fan scene to Beatlemania. The Tampa run marks the largest K-pop concert event in Florida history. 'SWIM' simultaneously tops the Billboard Global 200 for a fourth consecutive week.

media.caption: BTS opens North American leg of the ARIRANG World Tour at Raymond James Stadium, Tampa, April 25, 2026

events.title: BTS Brings ARIRANG Tour to Latin America — Mexico City at Estadio GNP Seguros (May 7, 9, 10)
events.detail: BTS arrives in Mexico City in May 2026 for three sold-out shows at Estadio GNP Seguros (formerly Estadio Azul) — dates: May 7, 9, and 10 at 8:00 PM local time. The Latin American leg marks BTS's return to Mexico City for the first time since their 2019 Speak Yourself tour. The 360-degree in-the-round stage configuration — BTS's signature for the ARIRANG World Tour — is deployed at GNP Seguros with four cross-shaped extended walkways, providing clear sightlines from all sections. The three-night run draws approximately 105,000 fans total, representing an unprecedented K-pop event in Mexico City's modern concert history. Fan enthusiasm across Latin America reaches a level comparable to North American and European legs, with ARMY communities across Mexico, Argentina, Brazil, Chile, and Colombia converging on the capital. Infobae Mexico, Milenio, and other major Spanish-language outlets provide wall-to-wall coverage, reflecting BTS's outsized cultural footprint in Spanish-speaking markets.

media.caption: BTS's ARIRANG World Tour Latin American leg at Estadio GNP Seguros, Mexico City — May 7, 9, 10, 2026

events.title: Day 4,700 Since Debut — ARIRANG North America Tour Confirmed at 31 Shows / 12 Cities; 'SWIM' Reaches New Airplay Peak
events.detail: April 26, 2026 marks exactly 4,700 days since BTS's June 13, 2013 debut — coinciding with Tampa Night 2 of the ARIRANG World Tour. Coverage published on April 26 by Korea Herald, Korea Times, STARNEWS Korea, and IBTimes AU confirms the full North American tour scope: 31 concerts across 12 cities including El Paso, Mexico City, New York, and additional dates added in Tampa, Stanford (CA), and Las Vegas due to overwhelming demand. Economic impact for the Tampa region is projected at $800M–$900M. Simultaneously, Soompi and Billboard report 'SWIM' climbs to a new peak of No. 13 on Billboard Pop Radio Airplay — BTS's highest-ever position on that survey and the highest by any Korean act in history. ARIRANG becomes the first album by a Korean artist to spend four consecutive weeks in the top 3 of the Billboard 200.

media.caption: On Day 4,700 since debut, BTS confirms 31-show North American ARIRANG tour and 'SWIM' reaches record-breaking No. 13 on Pop Radio Airplay

events.title: ARIRANG World Tour Night 1 in Mexico City — 60,000+ Fans, Surprise Songs, Profeco Fines Ticketmaster
events.detail: BTS opens the Latin American leg of the ARIRANG World Tour on May 7, 2026 at Estadio GNP Seguros in Mexico City — their first Mexico City performances since the 2019 Speak Yourself tour. The show draws over 60,000 fans, running approximately 8:15 PM to 10:20 PM local time with fire, pyrotechnics, and a 360-degree in-the-round stage. The setlist blends ARIRANG album tracks ('Hooligan,' 'Aliens,' '2.0,' 'NORMAL,' 'Body to Body') with classic hits ('Not Today,' 'MIC Drop,' 'IDOL,' 'Butter,' 'Dynamite') and two surprise songs: 'Boy in Luv' (2014) and 'So What' (2020) — the first live performances of both in over four years. BTS addressed the crowd in Spanish, English, and Korean. However, Night 1 was also marred by controversy: videos showing empty seats inside the venue went viral alongside clips of ARMY fans gathered outside unable to enter. Mexico's consumer protection agency Profeco initiated fine proceedings of more than 5 million pesos (~$277,800 USD) against Ticketmaster México for alleged legal violations during the ticket sale process. StubHub and Viagogo were also cited. Billboard described the situation as BTS's tour becoming 'a state affair' in Mexico. The three-night Mexico City run (May 7, 9, 10) is projected to draw 136,000+ total fans and represents the largest single-city K-pop concert event in Latin American history.

media.caption: BTS Night 1 at Estadio GNP Seguros, Mexico City — May 7, 2026: 60,000+ fans, pyrotechnics, surprise songs, Profeco fine against Ticketmaster

events.title: Prosecutors Reject Police Arrest Warrant for HYBE Chairman a Second Time — Travel Ban Continues
events.detail: South Korean prosecutors on May 7, 2026 rejected for the second time a Seoul Metropolitan Police Agency request for an arrest warrant against HYBE Chairman Bang Si-hyuk, citing insufficient supplementary investigation. The police had re-filed after an initial rejection in late April 2026. Bang faces allegations of deceiving early HYBE investors in 2019 by encouraging them to sell equity stakes at undervalue, allegedly generating approximately 260 billion KRW (~$179M USD) in illicit gains following the 2020 HYBE IPO. Bang has been under a travel ban since August 2025. The US Embassy reportedly sent a letter requesting permission for Bang to travel to attend the BTS ARIRANG World Tour abroad — a request prosecutors are still evaluating. Bang has denied all allegations. The second rejection may complicate further police action, though the investigation remains ongoing. Korea Times and Korea Herald confirmed the development on May 7 — the same night BTS performed Night 1 in Mexico City.

media.caption: Prosecutors reject for a second time the police arrest warrant request for HYBE Chairman Bang Si-hyuk — May 7, 2026

events.title: ARIRANG World Tour Mexico City Grand Finale — Night 3 Closes 136,000+ Fan Run; 'Spring Day' Tour Debut; BTS Visit Arena México
events.detail: BTS closes the Mexico City leg of the ARIRANG World Tour on May 10, 2026 with the grand finale at Estadio GNP Seguros — the third of three sold-out nights completing a 136,000+ fan run that stands as the largest K-pop stadium event in Latin American history. Night 3 is the most emotionally charged of the three performances. RM delivers an extended farewell address in Spanish. 'Spring Day' receives its live debut on the ARIRANG World Tour, producing one of the tour's loudest crowd reactions. V's closing farewell — 'México, los llevamos en el corazón para siempre' ('Mexico, we carry you in our hearts forever') — goes viral on Weverse within minutes of the show's end. Billboard describes the GNP Seguros run as 'the defining K-pop event of 2026.' Earlier in the day, Jin and three other BTS members attend a lucha libre event at Arena México, where pro-wrestler Místico wears a white BTS-embroidered jacket — a cross-cultural moment that resonates deeply with ARMY across Latin America and helps offset the negative press from the Ticketmaster controversy. The tour now advances to Las Vegas (Allegiant Stadium, May 23–28).

media.caption: BTS Night 3 grand finale at Estadio GNP Seguros — closing the 136,000+ fan Mexico City leg of the ARIRANG World Tour, May 10, 2026

events.title: HYBE × Geffen Reveals Global Girl Group 'SAINT SATINE' — Four-Member Lineup Unveiled at Survival Show Finale
events.detail: On May 12, 2026, HYBE × Geffen Records reveals SAINT SATINE — their new global girl group — in the finale of 'World Scout: The Final Piece' airing on ABEMA. The four-member lineup: Emily (USA, 20), Lexie (Sweden, 21), Samara (Brazil, 20), and Sakura (Japan, 15). Sakura was selected from over 14,000 global applicants as the final member via the survival format. Two debut tracks — 'WE RIDE' and 'PARTY B4 THE PARTY' — were released globally on streaming platforms the same day. Three members (Emily, Lexie, Samara) previously appeared in Pop Star Academy: KATSEYE. SAINT SATINE is HYBE's most prominent Western-facing act after KATSEYE and arrives during BTS's ARIRANG World Tour peak revenue period.

events.title: ARIRANG World Tour Projected to Gross $1.8 Billion — Stanford Stadium Debut Three Days Away
events.detail: On May 13, 2026 — Day 4,717 since BTS's debut — StarNews Korea reports that the ARIRANG World Tour is now projected to gross approximately $1.8 billion across 79 shows in 34 regions, which would rank it among the highest-grossing concert tours in music history. BTS is in transit to the San Francisco Bay Area for three sold-out shows at Stanford Stadium (May 16, 17, and 19). The group will become only the second musical act to ever perform at the 50,000-capacity venue, after Coldplay. On the Billboard charts, 'SWIM' rebounds to No. 1 on the Billboard Global (Excl. US) chart and holds No. 2 on the Global 200, while five BTS albums chart simultaneously on the World Albums chart. The $1.8B projection comes on the heels of HYBE's record Q1 2026 revenue of ~$478M — largely driven by ARIRANG World Tour merchandise, streaming, and Weverse subscriptions. After Stanford, the tour advances to Allegiant Stadium in Las Vegas (May 23–28) alongside the 'BTS: The City Arirang' citywide festival.

media.caption: ARIRANG World Tour $1.8B revenue projection — BTS Stanford Stadium debut in 3 days, May 13, 2026

events.title: BTS, Madonna & Shakira Confirmed for 2026 FIFA World Cup Final Halftime Show — HYBE Stock Surges 7.2%
events.detail: On May 14, 2026, FIFA officially confirms BTS, Madonna, and Shakira as co-headliners for the first-ever halftime show at the FIFA World Cup Final, scheduled for July 19, 2026 at MetLife Stadium in East Rutherford, New Jersey. The performance is curated by Global Citizen with a goal of raising $100 million for the FIFA Global Citizen Education Fund. CNN, the Washington Post, Billboard, and CNBC all report on the confirmation. HYBE's stock surged 7.2% on the Korea Exchange, adding approximately 700 billion won (~$470 million USD) in market capitalization in a single session — the largest single-day HYBE stock movement of 2026. The halftime show booking places BTS alongside global icons Madonna and Shakira on the world's most-watched sporting stage, representing one of the most significant event booking milestones in the group's history. The announcement arrives as BTS is physically en route to Stanford Stadium for the Bay Area leg of the ARIRANG World Tour.

media.caption: BTS, Madonna, and Shakira confirmed as co-headliners for the 2026 FIFA World Cup Final halftime show at MetLife Stadium — May 14, 2026

events.title: ARIRANG World Tour Las Vegas — 4 Nights at Allegiant Stadium, ~260,000 Fans
events.detail: BTS performs four sold-out nights at Allegiant Stadium, Las Vegas (May 23, 24, 27, 28, 2026) — their second time headlining the venue (after Permission to Dance on Stage, 2022). The residency draws approximately 260,000 fans across the four shows, all sold out in 23 minutes when on sale in April. The 11-day 'BTS THE CITY ARIRANG Las Vegas' citywide fan experience runs May 21–31 alongside the concerts, featuring a Samsung Galaxy × BTS fan activation, ARIRANG visual installations across the Strip, and a BTS pop-up at The Forum Shops at Caesars Palace. On May 25 (a rest day between shows), BTS attends the 52nd American Music Awards at MGM Grand Garden Arena — their first US award show appearance in four years — winning Artist of the Year, Song of the Summer ('SWIM'), and Best Male K-Pop Artist. The Las Vegas residency concludes the North American leg of the ARIRANG World Tour, which grossed an estimated $800M+ across 25 cities in Canada, the US, and Mexico.

media.caption: BTS ARIRANG World Tour Las Vegas — 4 sold-out nights at Allegiant Stadium (~260,000 fans), May 23–28, 2026

events.title: BTS Wins 3 Awards at 52nd AMAs — Artist of the Year, Song of the Summer, Best Male K-Pop
events.detail: On May 25, 2026 (Memorial Day), BTS wins three awards at the 52nd American Music Awards held at MGM Grand Garden Arena in Las Vegas — their first US televised award show appearance in approximately four years. Hosted by Queen Latifah and airing live on CBS, the ceremony sees BTS claim: Artist of the Year (beating Taylor Swift, Bad Bunny, Bruno Mars, and others), Song of the Summer ('SWIM'), and Best Male K-Pop Artist. Jin accepts the Artist of the Year award on behalf of the group; Jimin accepts Song of the Summer. The wins raise BTS's all-time AMA total to 14 — the most of any act in AMA history, surpassing Taylor Swift's record. The convergence of the ARIRANG World Tour Las Vegas residency with the AMAs marks one of the most prominent single-week stretches in BTS's post-hiatus career.

media.caption: BTS wins Artist of the Year, Song of the Summer, and Best Male K-Pop at the 52nd AMAs — first US award show in four years, May 25, 2026

events.title: BTS FESTA 2026 Begins — 13-Day Countdown to 13th Debut Anniversary
events.detail: On June 1, 2026, Big Hit Music launches BTS FESTA 2026 on Weverse — the annual two-week anniversary celebration counting down to June 13, the group's 13th debut anniversary. This is the first FESTA conducted during an active world tour. The FESTA schedule includes a family photo drop (June 4), the official 'Hooligan' performance video (June 5) timed to the opening of 'BTS THE CITY ARIRANG Busan,' and a Weverse Live anniversary session. Anniversary concerts at Busan Asiad Main Stadium on June 12–13 — BTS's debut city — will be streamed globally via Trafalgar Releasing cinema live viewing on June 13. Nike By You × BTS ARIRANG and BTS × Oreo hotteok cookies both launch on June 1, adding brand momentum to the FESTA opening.

media.caption: BTS FESTA 2026 begins June 1 — 13-day countdown to 13th debut anniversary; concerts at Busan Asiad Main Stadium June 12–13

events.title: BTS FESTA 2026 Family Photo — First Full Group Anniversary Shot Post-Military Service
events.detail: On June 4, 2026 (FESTA Day 4), Big Hit Music releases the official BTS FESTA 2026 Family Photo — the 13th consecutive annual anniversary photo tradition. The 2026 edition is the first with all seven members fully reunited since completing mandatory military service. Photos show all members in casual business attire on a sunlit outdoor lawn, with a behind-the-scenes video released simultaneously on Weverse. The photos trend globally under #BTSFamiPhoto2026 in 40+ countries, with ARMY noting the joyful, relaxed dynamic that marks BTS's post-reunion era.

media.caption: BTS FESTA 2026 Family Photo — June 4, 2026: first full seven-member anniversary photoshoot since military service completion

events.title: 'BTS THE CITY ARIRANG Busan' Opens; 'Hooligan' Performance Video Released — FESTA Day 5
events.detail: June 5, 2026 (FESTA Day 5): two major milestones coincide. 'BTS THE CITY ARIRANG Busan' opens across multiple city locations — a citywide fan festival running through June 21, featuring a drone light show over Gwangan Bridge, an ARIRANG exhibition at Shinsegae Centum City, and an ARMY MADANG fan community plaza at The Bay 101. Busan designates June 5–13 as 'BTS WEEK' with purple landmark lighting and BTS-branded public transport. Simultaneously, Big Hit Music releases the official performance video for 'Hooligan' — the tour's signature opening track — on Bangtan TV YouTube. Both activations serve as countdown pieces to the June 12–13 Busan Asiad Main Stadium anniversary concerts (7 days away), with a projected local economic impact exceeding 600 billion KRW (~$420M USD) during BTS WEEK.

media.caption: BTS THE CITY ARIRANG Busan opens June 5 alongside the 'Hooligan' performance video release — 7 days before the Busan Asiad Main Stadium anniversary concerts

events.title: 'SWIM' Ties 'Dynamite' — 8 Consecutive Weeks at No. 1, Billboard Global (Excl. US)
events.detail: On the chart dated June 6, 2026, BTS's 'SWIM' reaches its 8th consecutive week at No. 1 on the Billboard Global (Excl. US) chart — officially tying 'Dynamite' (2020) for BTS's longest-ever run at the top of that chart. 'SWIM' simultaneously rises from No. 10 to No. 4 on the Billboard Global 200. BTS now holds 8 total No. 1 leaders on Billboard Global (Excl. US), double nearest competitors. The milestone coincides with FESTA Day 7 content: 'Normal Log' released on Weverse, with anniversary song re-releases ('Never Let Go' by JK, 'Bicycle' by RM, 'Dear. ARMY' live clip by Jimin) launched across streaming platforms. Busan Asiad Main Stadium anniversary concerts are 5 days away.

media.caption: 'SWIM' ties 'Dynamite' with 8 consecutive weeks at No. 1 on Billboard Global Excl. US — chart dated June 6, 2026

events.title: BTS Closes FESTA 2026 With 13th Anniversary Homecoming at Busan Asiad Stadium
events.detail: BTS closes BTS FESTA 2026 with two nights at Busan Asiad Main Stadium (June 12-13), their first return to the city since 'Yet To Come in Busan' (2022) — the show remembered as their final concert before enlistment. The two nights draw roughly 220,000 fans combined, with about 110,000 attending the June 13 finale on the exact 13th debut anniversary. Busan holds special meaning as the hometown of Jimin and Jungkook; the members addressed the crowd about the emotional significance of returning as a full group.

media.caption: BTS closes their 13th anniversary FESTA with an emotional two-night homecoming at Busan Asiad Main Stadium.

events.title: ARIRANG World Tour European Leg Wraps in Paris With Record 92,000-Fan Finale
events.detail: BTS closes the European leg of the ARIRANG World Tour with two nights at Stade de France in Paris (July 17-18), drawing roughly 92,000 fans per show — the highest single-show attendance of any BTS concert to date. Across five cities (Madrid, Brussels, London, Munich, Paris) the group played 10 shows to a combined 717,000-720,000 fans, becoming the first Korean act to headline Brussels' King Baudouin Stadium and Munich's Allianz Arena, while their two nights at London's Tottenham Hotspur Stadium set that venue's highest-attendance record. Every city sold out in under 45 minutes.

media.caption: BTS wraps the European leg of the ARIRANG World Tour with a record 92,000-fan finale at Paris's Stade de France.

events.title: BTS Performs 'Dynamite' at First-Ever FIFA World Cup Final Halftime Show
events.detail: BTS takes the field at the FIFA World Cup Final in New Jersey for the tournament's first-ever halftime show, performing 'Dynamite' alongside sets from Madonna, Justin Bieber, and Shakira (feat. Burna Boy). The Chris Martin-curated, Global Citizen-produced show features conductor Gustavo Dudamel, the New York Philharmonic, and the Simón Bolívar Symphony Orchestra of Venezuela; BTS joins all performers for Coldplay's original closing song 'We Dance.' The appearance caps a 48-hour turnaround after wrapping the ARIRANG World Tour's European leg in Paris.

media.caption: BTS performs 'Dynamite' at the first-ever FIFA World Cup Final halftime show.

events.title: HYBE Posts Record Q2 2026 Revenue, Driven by BTS's ARIRANG World Tour
events.detail: HYBE reports consolidated Q2 2026 revenue of ₩1.45 trillion (~$1.0B) and operating profit of ₩170.9 billion, up 105.5% YoY and 107.6% QoQ — its best quarter on record. Concert revenue surges 630.0% QoQ and 243.3% YoY to ₩647.7 billion (~$432M), which the company attributes directly to BTS's ARIRANG World Tour. CEO Lee Jae-sang credits the tour and balanced roster growth. ARIRANG was also the top-selling vinyl and CD release in the U.S. for the first half of 2026.

media.caption: HYBE posts record Q2 2026 revenue, with concert revenue up 243% YoY on the strength of BTS's ARIRANG World Tour.

events.title: BTS Declines to Submit ARIRANG for 2027 Grammy Consideration
events.detail: BTS announces via Instagram it will not submit music for 2027 Grammy consideration, about a month after the Recording Academy introduced a new 'Best Asian Pop Music Performance' category among five new categories for the 69th Grammys. "We have decided not to submit an entry for Grammy consideration this year," the group wrote. "We hope music can be heard and loved for what it is, rather than being divided by region or language." The statement doesn't name the category directly, but its timing and language drew wide comparisons to criticism that the category sidelines K-pop and other Asian acts from the main categories, where BTS has 5 nominations and no wins.

media.caption: BTS says it will not submit ARIRANG for 2027 Grammy consideration following the Recording Academy's new Asian Pop category.

events.title: 'BTS ARMY: Forever We Are Young' Documentary Opens in Theaters Worldwide
events.detail: The fan documentary 'BTS ARMY: Forever We Are Young,' directed by Grace Lee and Patty Anh, opens in theaters worldwide via Trafalgar Releasing. The film follows ARMY members across continents, exploring the fandom's passion, creativity, and activism rather than focusing on the group itself.

media.caption: 'BTS ARMY: Forever We Are Young' opens in theaters worldwide, spotlighting the fandom's global impact.

events.title: ARIRANG World Tour Returns to North America With Two Nights at MetLife Stadium
events.detail: BTS opens the North American return leg of the ARIRANG World Tour with two nights at MetLife Stadium in East Rutherford, NJ (Aug 1-2) — the same venue as the World Cup Final halftime show two weeks earlier. The shows feature a 360-degree rotating stage inspired by traditional Korean architecture, blending ARIRANG-era tracks ('Hooligan,' 'Aliens,' 'SWIM,' 'Body to Body') with catalogue staples ('Butter,' 'Dynamite,' 'IDOL,' 'FAKE LOVE,' 'MIC Drop,' 'Fire').

media.caption: BTS opens the North American return leg of the ARIRANG World Tour with two sold-out nights at MetLife Stadium.

events.title: ARIRANG World Tour Debuts at Gillette Stadium, Foxborough
events.detail: BTS performs at Gillette Stadium in Foxborough, MA for the first time (Aug 5-6), marking the largest headlining K-pop shows ever held at the venue. The in-the-round staging places the audience at the center of the show as the ARIRANG World Tour's North American return leg continues after the MetLife Stadium opener.

media.caption: BTS makes its first appearance at Gillette Stadium, the largest headlining K-pop show in the venue's history.

events.title: Toronto City Council Approves Temporary 'BTS Boulevard' Street Renaming
events.detail: Toronto City Council adopts a motion to temporarily co-name a stretch of Yonge Street 'BTS Boulevard' (Aug 21-Sep 23), welcoming ARMY ahead of BTS's Rogers Stadium shows (Aug 22-23). Council also asks Mayor Olivia Chow to proclaim 'BTS Weekend' and requests City Hall's sign be lit purple for the concert dates.

media.caption: Toronto City Council approves temporarily renaming part of Yonge Street 'BTS Boulevard' ahead of the group's Rogers Stadium shows.

events.title: ARIRANG World Tour Opens Two-Night Baltimore Run at M&T Bank Stadium
events.detail: BTS brings the ARIRANG World Tour's North American return leg to M&T Bank Stadium in Baltimore for two nights (Aug 10-11). Maryland Governor Wes Moore welcomes the group with a video message praising their mission of "bringing the world together and transcending cultural, geographical and language barriers." The stop precedes shows at AT&T Stadium in Arlington (Aug 15-16) and Rogers Stadium in Toronto (Aug 22-23).

media.caption: BTS's ARIRANG World Tour sweeps North America, with Baltimore's two-night M&T Bank Stadium run drawing a welcome message from Maryland Governor Wes Moore.

events.title: ARIRANG World Tour Closes Two-Night Baltimore Stand at M&T Bank Stadium
events.detail: BTS closes its two-night Baltimore run at M&T Bank Stadium with a second sold-out show, a night after a tornado warning and severe thunderstorms forced fans to shelter inside the stadium and delayed gate openings. The Baltimore Sun and Fox Baltimore report the shows drew ARMY from as far as Mexico, Florida, and Ohio, giving Charm City businesses a significant tourism boost, with city officials hoping to convert first-time visitors into repeat tourists. A Clutchpoints review of the run likened the atmosphere to Beatlemania and the 1964 British Invasion.

media.caption: BTS fans travel from Mexico, Florida, and Ohio for Baltimore's two sold-out M&T Bank Stadium shows, boosting local business.

events.title: 'SWIM' Ties 'Butter' for BTS's Longest-Ever Hot 100 Run at 20 Weeks
events.detail: 'SWIM' logs its 20th week on the Billboard Hot 100 (No. 91, chart dated Aug 15), tying 'Butter' (2021) for BTS's longest-charting Hot 100 song ever. The single also holds No. 4 on Billboard Global (Excl. US) and No. 12 on the Billboard Global 200. Parent album 'ARIRANG' marks its own 20th consecutive week on the Billboard 200, currently at No. 14 — a record run for a K-pop album.

media.caption: 'SWIM' ties 'Butter' for BTS's longest-ever Hot 100 run, at 20 consecutive weeks.

events.title: Dallas-Fort Worth Fan Events Kick Off Ahead of Arlington ARIRANG Shows
events.detail: August 14, 2026 — Ahead of BTS's two-night ARIRANG World Tour stop at AT&T Stadium (Aug 15-16), Dallas-Fort Worth ARMY events begin: Texas Live!'s 'Into the Boraverse' pre-concert event (free Aug 14 pre-party, paid Aug 15-16 with a live DJ), official merch pickup at Esports Stadium Arlington (Aug 14-16), and cupsleeve events across the metroplex.

media.caption: Dallas-Fort Worth ARMY fan events kick off ahead of BTS's Aug 15-16 AT&T Stadium shows.

events.title: Fans Begin Overnight Merch Line at Choctaw Stadium Ahead of Arlington Shows
events.detail: ARMY start lining up as early as 10 p.m. Thursday outside Choctaw Stadium in Arlington for official ARIRANG World Tour merchandise, ahead of BTS's two-night AT&T Stadium run (Aug 15-16). By 11 a.m. Friday the line had wrapped around the stadium; fans traveled from as far as Nebraska, Alabama, and Odessa, Texas, enduring forecast highs of 101°F.

media.caption: ARMY fans line up overnight outside Choctaw Stadium in Arlington for official ARIRANG merchandise ahead of BTS's AT&T Stadium shows.

events.title: ARIRANG World Tour Opens Two-Night AT&T Stadium Run in Arlington
events.detail: BTS opens a sold-out two-night stand at AT&T Stadium (capacity ~80,000) in Arlington, Texas, the tour's third Texas stop after El Paso in May. Per setlist.fm, the show runs 2 hours 10 minutes across 24 songs, opening with 'Hooligan' and closing an encore with 'Into the Sun.' The show follows an overnight merch line at nearby Choctaw Stadium and a forecast high of 101°F. Night two follows Aug 16, after which the tour advances to Rogers Stadium in Toronto (Aug 22-23).

media.caption: BTS opens a sold-out two-night run at AT&T Stadium in Arlington, Texas.

events.title: V Discloses Hearing Loss, Jungkook Reveals Shin Injury on Weverse Live
events.detail: During a joint Weverse Live, V disclosed reduced hearing in his right ear ('If the hearing in my left ear is at 100, it's only about 30 in my right'), a condition he says worsened during his military service and is now treating with medication and regular hospital visits. Jungkook said on the same stream that he is on the verge of a shin stress fracture from inflammation that has limited his movement on the ARIRANG tour's North American leg, and plans to seek treatment once the tour returns to Korea.

media.caption: Fans revisit old BTS clips after V reveals hearing difficulties in a Weverse Live with Jungkook.

events.title: ARIRANG World Tour Closes Two-Night AT&T Stadium Run in Arlington
events.detail: BTS closed its sold-out two-night stand at AT&T Stadium in Arlington with a 25-song set that swapped in 'Butterfly' and 'The Most Beautiful Moment in Life Pt. 2' for Night 1's 'Others' and 'Permission to Dance,' per setlist.fm. The stand capped a weekend that drew ARMY from Nebraska, Alabama, and beyond despite 101°F heat. The tour now heads to Rogers Stadium in Toronto (Aug 22-23) -- BTS's first Canadian shows since 2018 -- then Chicago's Soldier Field (Aug 27-28).

media.caption: BTS closes a sold-out two-night run at AT&T Stadium in Arlington, Texas.

events.title: J-Hope, RM Draw Backlash for Attending Chris Brown's Toronto Concert
events.detail: J-Hope and RM attended the second of two Toronto stops on Chris Brown and Usher's co-headlining 'R&B Tour' at Rogers Stadium, days before BTS's own two-night Rogers Stadium run (Aug 22-23). Photos posted to Brown's Instagram showed the pair posing with him, and fan videos captured them dancing along to his song 'Look at Me Now.' The appearance drew backlash from segments of the ARMY fanbase citing Brown's 2009 felony assault conviction involving Rihanna and his July 2026 guilty plea over a 2023 London nightclub attack; other fans defended the pair. Neither J-Hope, RM, nor HYBE issued a formal response.

media.caption: J-Hope and RM attend Chris Brown and Usher's Toronto concert, sparking fan debate.

events.title: 'SWIM' Earns Two 2026 MTV VMA Nominations — Song of the Year, Best K-Pop
events.detail: MTV announced its 2026 Video Music Award nominations, with BTS's 'SWIM' earning two nods: Song of the Year and Best K-Pop. In Song of the Year, 'SWIM' competes against Madonna & Sabrina Carpenter's 'Bring Your Love,' PinkPantheress & Zara Larsson's 'Stateside,' Raye's 'Where is My Husband!,' and HUNTR/X's 'Golden.' In Best K-Pop, 'SWIM' is up against BLACKPINK's 'Jump,' CORTIS, LE SSERAFIM's 'Spaghetti' (featuring J-Hope), Katseye, and Lisa's 'Dream.' The ceremony airs September 27, 2026 from the Peacock Theatre in Los Angeles.

media.caption: BTS's 'SWIM' earns 2026 MTV VMA nominations for Song of the Year and Best K-Pop.

events.title: Toronto ARMY Rallies Ahead of BTS's First Canadian Shows Since 2018
events.detail: With BTS's two-night Rogers Stadium stand two days out (Aug 22-23) — the group's first Canadian concerts since 2018 — local fan community BTS Army Toronto, run by Sokvin Vann and her son Jordan, describes a citywide buildup ARMY are calling a homecoming. 'It feels like a homecoming, right? From 2018 to the missed 2020 concert. Now eight years later, it feels like our seven kings are coming home,' Vann told reporters. Rogers Stadium is expected to draw roughly 100,000 fans across the two sold-out nights.

media.caption: BTS Army Toronto anticipates the group's first Canadian shows since 2018 at Rogers Stadium.

events.title: Toronto Renames Yonge Street 'BTS Boulevard,' Proclaims BTS Weekend as Fans Line Up for Merch
events.detail: Toronto installed 20 black-and-red 'BTS Boulevard' signs along Yonge Street in North York, between North York Boulevard and Finch Avenue, temporarily co-naming the strip through September 23 to welcome ARMY ahead of BTS's two sold-out Rogers Stadium concerts (Aug 22-23) — the group's first Toronto shows in over a decade. City Council, acting on a motion by Councillor Lily Cheng, asked Mayor Olivia Chow to proclaim August 22-23 'BTS Weekend,' inviting fans to wear purple; the Toronto Sign at Nathan Phillips Square was set to be illuminated in purple for the occasion. The designation coincides with the Toronto Korean Festival (Aug 21-23) at nearby Mel Lastman Square, billed as Canada's largest Korean cultural festival. Separately, thousands of fans lined up outside Rogers Stadium for official tour merchandise (ranging $85-$369), with one fan, Ella, describing arriving before 6 a.m. to a line stretching 'down to Downsview Station.' The TTC added extra Line 1 subway service and buses on routes 84, 984, and 101 for concertgoers.

A 'BTS Boulevard' sign installed on Yonge Street in North York, Toronto.

events.title: BTS Opens Toronto Rogers Stadium Stand After Storm Delay
events.detail: August 22, 2026 — BTS opened its two-night Rogers Stadium stand in Toronto — the group's first Canadian shows in over a decade and its only Canadian stop on the 88-show, 34-city ARIRANG World Tour. Environment Canada issued a yellow severe-thunderstorm warning as fans arrived; organizers evacuated roughly 50,000 fans from the grandstands to the fan plaza as thunder and heavy rain hit the outdoor Downsview venue. The storm cleared about three songs in and the show, delayed from its scheduled 8:00 p.m. start, began at 8:25 p.m. and ran to 10:35 p.m. across a 25-song, 360-degree in-the-round set. Fans — some who had traveled from as far as Niagara Falls — called it 'one of my favorite shows' despite the rain-soaked conditions. The visit coincided with the city's temporary 'BTS Boulevard' co-naming of a Yonge Street stretch and the Toronto Korean Festival.

media.caption: A fan wears a mask of BTS member Jin as fans arrive for the group's first of two Toronto concerts, Aug. 22, 2026.

events.title: BTS Closes Toronto Stand With Tour-Debut 'Zero O'Clock,' First 'Outro: Tear' Since 2019
events.detail: August 23, 2026 — BTS closed its two-night Rogers Stadium stand in Toronto with two setlist rarities: the ARIRANG World Tour debut of '00:00 (Zero O'Clock)' and the group's first live performance of 'Outro: Tear' since 2019, alongside the returning main set, per setlist.fm. The Fan Plaza opened at 4:30 p.m. and doors at 5:30 p.m. ahead of the roughly 8 p.m. start. The weekend stand — Canada's only stop on the 88-show, 34-city ARIRANG World Tour and BTS's first Toronto shows in 11 years — drew an estimated 100,000 fans across both nights to the specially built 360-degree in-the-round stage. The tour now advances to two nights at Chicago's Soldier Field (Aug 27-28).

media.caption: BTS fans fill Rogers Stadium in Toronto as the group wraps its only Canadian tour stop.

events.title: Illinois Governor Declares 'BTS Day' Ahead of Chicago Soldier Field Shows
events.detail: August 20, 2026 — Illinois Governor JB Pritzker proclaimed August 27-28 'BTS Day' in Illinois, honoring the group's two sold-out Soldier Field concerts — BTS's first Chicago shows in more than seven years. The proclamation, petitioned by the fan group Chicago BTS Army and the HANA Center (an Irving Park immigrant-advocacy nonprofit), states BTS 'has transcended international borders and utilizes their platform to champion social causes, including mental health awareness, self-love, and global philanthropy.' The two groups also launched a 'Borahae Purple' campaign — referencing the ARMY phrase 'I purple you' — to light Chicago's downtown skyline purple; Willis Tower is set to glow purple 8:30-11 p.m. on both concert nights, with fan gatherings planned at Buckingham Fountain and across Chinatown and Downtown.

media.caption: Illinois Gov. JB Pritzker cited BTS's global philanthropy in declaring 'BTS Day' ahead of the group's Soldier Field shows.

events.title: Chicago Guide Maps Fan Celebrations Ahead of Soldier Field Shows
events.detail: August 24, 2026 — Block Club Chicago published a citywide guide to ARMY celebrations ahead of BTS's two sold-out Soldier Field shows (Aug 27-28), cataloguing fan parties, pop-ups, giveaways and food specials planned across the city through the week. The guide highlighted Chinatown fan activities — including a concert-themed cupsleeve event at Uni Uni Chinatown and free raffles, bracelet-making, and BTS/BT21 coloring activities at Hello Jasmine — alongside the previously announced 'BTS Day' skyline lighting of Willis Tower (Aug 27-28, 8:30-11 p.m.) and Buckingham Fountain fan gatherings tied to Governor JB Pritzker's Illinois proclamation.

media.caption: ARMY fans prepare for BTS's return to Chicago ahead of two sold-out Soldier Field shows.

events.title: Early Merch Sale Opens in Chicago Ahead of Soldier Field Shows
events.detail: August 26, 2026 — Soldier Field opened early merchandise sales from 10 a.m. to 6 p.m. at the Waldron Deck and Stadium Green, offering free Waldron Deck parking to fans shopping ahead of BTS's two sold-out Soldier Field shows (Aug 27-28) — the group's first Chicago concerts in more than seven years, coinciding with Governor JB Pritzker's 'BTS Day' proclamation. Exterior merchandise locations open at 10 a.m. on both show days; parking lots open at 4 p.m., and the venue enforces a no-backpacks policy and cashless payments. Fans also gathered that evening for the 21+ 'ARMYRANG Chicago Pre-Party' at Bassline in the South Loop (10 p.m.-2 a.m.), part of a week of Chinatown and Downtown fan events tied to the shows.

media.caption: BTS's ARIRANG World Tour arrives in Chicago for two sold-out Soldier Field shows.

events.title: Chicago's First Lady Hosts Sold-Out BTS Fireworks Cruise; CTA Releases Choreography Video
events.detail: Chicago's First Lady cruise line hosts a sold-out BTS-soundtracked fireworks cruise on Lake Michigan while the CTA releases a social media video of employees performing BTS choreography, part of the citywide buildup to the group's two sold-out Soldier Field shows (Aug 27-28) under Illinois's 'BTS Day' proclamation.

media.caption: BTS takes over Chicago ahead of sold-out Soldier Field concerts.

events.title: BTS Day 1 in Chicago: Fans Line Up at Dawn for Soldier Field Merch as 'BTS Day' Begins
events.detail: The first of BTS's two sold-out Soldier Field shows takes place under Illinois's 'BTS Day' proclamation. Fans line up at Soldier Field by 7 a.m. for exterior merchandise sales; the venue enforces a strict clear-bag policy and directs fans to CTA bus, 'L,' and Metra routes ahead of the 8 p.m. show — BTS's first Chicago concerts in more than seven years.
